leads.name: Arbre botella del Botanic II
leads.reason: Only one source found this pass: the official register itself. No independent article, garden-authority page or Wikipedia entry specific to this individual specimen turned up. Species-name ambiguity noted: the Jardi Botanic's own public catalogue page found in this pass describes a 'arbol botella' / Brachychiton DISCOLOR (not populneus) in the same garden, and both species share the Spanish common name 'arbol botella' (bottle tree), so it is unclear whether the register's populneus ID for this exact specimen is correct or whether the web description refers to a different bottle tree in the garden. Needs either a second independent source for this specific register point, or an in-person/photo check of the trunk and leaf shape to resolve the species question before this can be delivered as verified.

leads.name: The Ficus of the Corts Valencianes
leads.why: PULLED FROM THE LIVE PAGE 2026-08-29 on hard rule 10. Inside the working seat of the Valencian regional parliament, visible only on a free guided tour that must be booked in advance, is not offered in August, and which the entry itself called not a walk-up, casual-visit tree. Nothing is wrong with the tree and the research is kept here in full; it can go back the day the access changes. Access as published: RESTRICTED: this is the working seat of the Valencian regional parliament (Corts Valencianes), inside the Palau de Benicarlo / Palau dels Borja. The garden and ficus are visible only on a free guided tour, offered Mondays and Fridays mornings at 10:00/11:00/12:00/13:00, must be booked in advance by phone or the Corts Valencianes website, and NOT offered in August. This is not a walk-up, casual-visit tree.
leads.age_estimate: sources disagree: called both 'century-old' and dated to the second half of the 19th century
leads.story:
One of the largest fig trees in Valencia grows in a garden you can enter twice a week, by appointment, and not at all in August. It stands in the courtyard of the Palau de Benicarlo, also known as the Palau dels Borja, which is the working seat of the Corts Valencianes, the Valencian regional parliament. The only way to stand under it is the free guided tour of the building, offered on Monday and Friday mornings and booked in advance through the parliament itself. The tour runs about an hour and spends most of it on the debating chamber rather than the garden, which is worth knowing before you go.

The tree is in the same weight class as the city's famous ones. The regional register measures its trunk at 13.6 metres around, within centimetres of El Titan in the Parterre. Its age is disputed. One account calls it simply a century old, 22 metres tall with a crown spreading more than 12 metres. Another dates its origins to the second half of the nineteenth century, which would make it something between 127 and 176. Both figures are in circulation and neither has a planting record behind it.

So this is the least casual visit on the list, and the only tree here that requires a phone call. It also spends its life inside a security perimeter, tended by a government that lists it as one of the region's monumental trees.

blocked.name: Ficus del Palacio de Raga (interior)
blocked.reason: PRIVATE LAND, not open to visitors. Stands inside the walled courtyard of the former Palacio de Raga, which today is a Generalitat Valenciana residencia (RPM Palau de Raga), a social-services care home and day centre for the elderly, not a museum or venue with public opening hours. Local legend holds it is the older and larger of the two Raga-area ficus (a supposed gift from botanist Cavanilles, which if true would put it over 200 years old), but it cannot be visited and its location is inside a residential care facility, which this project does not publish per hard rule 10. The PUBLIC tree 30m away in the same plaza is delivered as vlc_011; do not confuse the two.
